record.original_question: Suppose two geproci point sets have isomorphic matroids. Must they be projectively equivalent? More generally, is the property of being geproci determined purely by the associated matroid, so that any point set with a matroid isomorphic to that of a geproci set is itself geproci?

evidence.quote: Question 3.9. Are geproci sets with isomorphic matroids projectively equivalent? Is being geproci a property of the associated matroids, i.e., is a set of points whose matroid is isomorphic to the matroid of a geproci set, geproci itself?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Working in projective 3-space $\mathbb{P}^3$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, call a finite set of points $Z \subset \mathbb{P}^3$ a geproci set if there exist integers $a \le b$ such that, for a general point $p \in \mathbb{P}^3$, the image of $Z$ under linear projection from $p$ to a plane $\mathbb{P}^2$ is a complete intersection of curves of degrees $a$ and $b$ (in particular $|Z| = ab$). To any finite set of points $Z$ in a projective space one associates its (linear) matroid $M(Z)$, whose ground set is $Z$ and whose independent sets are the projectively independent subsets of $Z$; two point sets $Z, Z'$ are said to have isomorphic matroids if there is a bijection between them preserving independence. Two finite point sets $Z, Z' \subset \mathbb{P}^3$ are projectively equivalent if there is a linear automorphism of $\mathbb{P}^3$ carrying $Z$ to $Z'$.

(a) If two geproci sets $Z, Z' \subset \mathbb{P}^3$ have isomorphic matroids, must $Z$ and $Z'$ be projectively equivalent?

(b) Is the property of being geproci determined by the matroid: that is, if $Z \subset \mathbb{P}^3$ is a finite set whose matroid is isomorphic to the matroid of some geproci set, must $Z$ itself be geproci?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches surface discussions of geproci sets and their matroids (notably Oberwolfach reports and follow-up works), but no result asserts a proof or counterexample that geproci sets with isomorphic matroids must be projectively equivalent, nor that the geproci property is purely matroidal. The question is described as analogous to Terao's conjecture and appears to still be open.
